Trending
TREND-ing
adjective / verb (Millennial slang)
From trend (to turn, to extend in a direction; from Old English trendan, to revolve). The modern sense of trending, currently popular or much discussed online, came with Twitter’s "Trending Topics" (2008–2009), which listed the subjects most mentioned at the moment; hashtags trended, and appearing on the list became a marker of cultural importance. By the 2010s anything popular was "trending," and platforms built algorithms to surface it.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

To be trending is to be what everyone is talking about right now: the topic at the top of the list, the song in every video, the opinion that dominates the feed. Trends rise in hours and vanish in days. The Christian observation: Scripture has thought hard about the multitude. "Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil" (Exo 23:2). The trend is a crowd in motion, and crowds are not reliable guides. The same crowd that cried "Hosanna" cried "Crucify him" within a week; the trending opinion in Jerusalem on Good Friday was wrong. Paul warned of a time when people "will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears" (2Ti 4:3): itching ears are ears that want whatever is new. The Athenians "spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell, or to hear some new thing" (Act 17:21), a perfect description of a trending-topics culture. Not every trend is evil; some are harmless fun, and sometimes the crowd notices something true. But the Christian’s compass cannot be the trend list. "Be not conformed to this world" (Rom 12:2). A father teaches his children to ask of every trend: is it true, is it good, and would I care about it if no one else did? He shows them that faithfulness to God is never trending and always right.

Webster 1828 Definition

Millennial internet sense (Twitter Trending Topics, 2008–2009) of being currently popular online; Scripture forbids following a multitude to do evil (Exo 23:2) and diagnoses the itching ears that live for the new (2Ti 4:3; Act 17:21).

expand to see more

TRENDING, adj. / pres. part. (Millennial internet sense, 2008–present) Currently popular or widely discussed online, especially on a platform’s trending list. "It’s trending." Related: trending topic, hashtag.

Webster (1828), root trend: TREND, verb intransitive [This word seems to be allied to trundle, or to run.] To run; to stretch; to tend; to have a particular direction; as, the shore of the sea trends to the southwest.

Decode for parents: teach your children to test trends by truth, not by numbers.

Exo 23:2 — "Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil; neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to wrest judgment:"

2Ti 4:3 — "For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;"

Act 17:21 — "(For all the Athenians and strangers which were there spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell, or to hear some new thing.)"

Rom 12:2 — "And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God."

Modern Corruption

Trending makes the crowd’s momentary attention the measure of importance; Scripture forbids following the multitude and warns against itching ears.

expand to see more

The corruption is popularity as authority. The trending list tells users not only what is being discussed but implicitly what matters, and algorithms amplify whatever already has momentum. Young people learn to orient themselves by what is trending: opinions, causes, fashions, outrages. The crowd becomes the conscience. Jesus warned that the broad way is crowded: "wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat" (Mat 7:13).

The recovery is a fixed compass. Christians can notice trends, enjoy harmless ones, and engage the culture’s conversations; but they test everything by the Word and are prepared to stand alone. Teach the young that truth is not decided by volume, that the Church has often been right when it was unpopular, and that the most important things, the gospel, faithfulness, love of neighbour, never trend for long and never go out of date.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English trendan (to turn, revolve) → trend (to extend in a direction; a general tendency) → 2008–2009 Twitter "Trending Topics" → 2010s trending.

expand to see more

Old English trendan — to turn about, to revolve

16th–19th c.: trend — to run in a direction; a general tendency

2008–2009: Twitter’s "Trending Topics"

2010s: trending = currently popular; algorithmic amplification

Biblical anchor: thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil (Exo 23:2); itching ears (2Ti 4:3)
